mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below the previous quarter's value indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage inflation and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy with declining inflation, which can lead to a short-term equity pullback due to higher rates and uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in HOUST and GDPC1 on a month-over-month basis signals rising housing and overall demand activity, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: PAYEMS rising while UNRATE is flat or falling over three months indicates firms are adding workers without wage pressure, which supports profit margins and justifies positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE is flat or falls for three months
regime_hint: labor market loosening with employment growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: RSAFS rising above its 12-month moving average while GDPC1 is flat signals increased household savings without corresponding demand growth, which typically precedes a consumer spending slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average and GDPC1 flat
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered quarters.
